solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Talk about Latin reading exercise

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the next one, so it sits inside

parts.note: coze is an old word for a friendly chat
standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A teacher chatting about a Latin text in a reading class.
explanation.walkthrough: COZE wraps around L: CLOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloze test is a comprehension exercise in which the reader fills in words deleted from a passage.

clue.text: Ancient boxer's glove estimated to cut most of advantage

indicators.note: to cut into a word is to sit inside it, splitting it in two
taking most of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: cause in the sense of sake or interest, as in 'for the cause of'
standard abbreviation for estimated

explanation.surface: A historian guesses that the old boxing glove cut down much of a fighter's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advantage' here is cause in the old sense of sake or benefit, as in 'for the cause of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The caestus was a leather hand-covering, often weighted with metal, worn by boxers in ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Accepting onset of Parkinsonism, load up this treatment

indicators.note: a word accepting something takes it in among its own letters
letters that are up are stirred up or disturbed, so they get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its very beginning, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the disease's name

explanation.surface: Instructions to load up a drug for someone at the start of Parkinson's.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the drug really is loaded up for patients once Parkinson's begins.
explanation.definitionFit: L-dopa (levodopa) is the standard drug used to treat the symptoms of Parkinson's disease.

clue.text: You go now to get hubby? Spend stocks

parts.note: radio users say 'over' to hand the turn to speak to the other person
to fish for a husband is to try to catch one

explanation.surface: A wife dismissing her husband to the shops, then telling him to spend on stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose sense of fishing as hunting for a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To overfish is to deplete fish stocks by catching too many, so the stocks are spent or exhausted.

clue.text: Go with rank: not difficult to make detachment

definitions.note: describes the answer, an adjective for something easily detached

parts.note: zip means energy or vim, as does go
rank food has gone off, that is bad

explanation.surface: Advice to go along with authority so that leaving is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a position in a hierarchy; here it means smelly or rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A zip-off garment part, such as a hood or trouser leg, is fastened by a zip so it can be detached with ease.

clue.text: Spritely gran keeps going round massive sheds

indicators.note: a sprightly person is lively and moving about, so the letters jump into a new order
something going round another thing encloses it

parts.note: to keep something is to have it
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively grandmother keeps walking around some huge sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS goes round the shuffled GRAN: HA-NGAR-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangars are the very large buildings in which aircraft are housed and serviced.

clue.text: Old English rulers, amongst others — this chapter's to be revised

indicators.note: text that is to be revised will be rewritten and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, including the S

explanation.surface: An editor notes that a history book's chapter on early English kings must be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amongst others' is part of the definition: each such ruler was one of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Heptarchy was the seven Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of early England, and its kings were heptarchists, each ruling alongside six others.

clue.text: Those in cultured societies are blighters about nice aim flopping

indicators.note: something flopping falls about loosely, so its letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: A is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: a cad is a rotter or blighter
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneer at high society members as bounders whose good intentions fail.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then CADS around the shuffled NICE AIM: A-CAD-EMICIAN-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Academicians are elected members of learned academies, such as the Royal Academy, which are societies of culture.

clue.text: Emperor and unit of Chinese distilled fragrance

parts.note: the Roman emperor
the li is a Chinese unit of distance

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler and a Chinese measure combine in a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli is an essential oil distilled from bitter-orange blossom and used in perfumery.

clue.text: Grab article Royal Navy installed — hoisting gear

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside the other piece

parts.note: to grab something is to get it
the indefinite article
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sailor seizes an item the Navy has fitted to its lifting tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: GET holds A and RN: G-ARN-ET. The surface suggests the gemstone; here it is nautical tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnet is a kind of tackle on a ship used for hoisting cargo.

clue.text: Dash round Chicagoans' transport for reception

indicators.note: one word placed round another encloses it

parts.note: in printing a dash is a rule, as in an em rule
the El is Chicago's elevated railway

explanation.surface: Rushing around the Chicago transit system to get to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A rule is printers' name for a dash, as in an em rule; 'reception' is the old French bedroom gathering, not a hotel desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruelle was a morning reception held in a fine lady's bedroom in seventeenth-century France.

clue.text: Inquire about present in this paraffle fae the future wifie?

indicators.note: letters turned about are moved around into a new order

parts.note: speer (or speir) is Scots for to ask or inquire

explanation.surface: A Scots question about a gift on display from a bride-to-be.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a paraffle is a showy display and 'fae the future wifie' means from the bride-to-be: think of a hen night. The question mark marks this loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a lively, extravagant bout of fun, like the riotous night out a bride has before her wedding.

clue.text: Hype in place of sound counsel

parts.note: an ad (advertisement) is promotional hype
the Latin vice means in place of, as in vice-captain

explanation.surface: A plea for honest guidance instead of marketing spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance given about what to do, and good advice is sound counsel.

clue.text: Local river sheep get stuck in (5, two words)

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or stream
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A sheep becomes stuck in a nearby river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuck in' seems to describe the sheep's plight, but it is the British idiom for tucking in to food.
explanation.definitionFit: Get stuck in is British slang for starting something with gusto, including eating heartily.

clue.text: Special athlete from 'Ackney is relatively full of mineral

indicators.note: a Cockney from Hackney drops the H sound, as the apostrophe in the place name shows

parts.note: sp. is an abbreviation for special
a harrier is a cross-country runner

explanation.surface: A star runner from East London is said to be rich in minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of East London; Cockney speech drops the initial H. 'Relatively' asks for a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparry means rich in spar, a crystalline mineral, so the comparative form means containing comparatively more of it.

clue.text: Shoot jet circling close to destroyer

indicators.note: something circling another thing surrounds it

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: final letter of the warship

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft flies around near a naval destroyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' sounds military beside 'destroyer', but it is the plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a new shoot growing from a plant or seed.

clue.text: Agreed to install flipping large security device

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside

parts.note: 'Done!' is said to agree a deal

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it back to front

parts.note: standard abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly agrees to fit a big security system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' passes for a mild British curse, but it turns the abbreviation for large around.
explanation.definitionFit: A dongle is a small piece of hardware plugged into a computer, often to unlock licensed software.

clue.text: Rum — cheers, they made it one afternoon

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
ff. stands for fecerunt, Latin for they made it, signed on artworks
Roman numeral one
a. is an abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: A toast to the people who distilled a rum one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' could be the adjective meaning odd; here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tafia (taffia) is a cheap rum made in the West Indies from molasses or sugar refuse.

clue.text: In new composition I use flat calami

indicators.note: a new composition puts the parts together in a different arrangement

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer explains using a flat key in a new piece for reed pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' sounds musical; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calami and fistulae are both Latin plurals for reeds or pipes, such as the pipes of a reed instrument.

clue.text: I, with our feminist, made distinct agreements

indicators.note: making something distinct changes it into a different form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone and a feminist colleague drew up separate agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the anagram signal means 'made different', yet the answer means sameness.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformities are instances of sameness or consistency, which is agreement in the sense of correspondence.

clue.text: Yard is sheltered by kind architect's spacing of columns

indicators.note: something sheltered by another thing sits inside it

parts.note: a kind or type is a style
standard abbreviation
's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A courtyard protected by a gentle architect.
explanation.walkthrough: Y and 'S sit inside STYLE after its first letter: S-YS-TYLE. 'Kind' looks like an adjective but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Systyle is a classical architectural term for columns set two diameters apart.

clue.text: Oddly get wind of snap and credit note with hidden meaning

parts.note: to sus (suss) something is to find it out
a snap is a photo, a pic
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt
sly means artful or with something concealed

explanation.surface: Someone strangely uncovers a photo and an IOU carrying a coded message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' poses as an anagram signal at the front, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting oddly, in a way that arouses distrust, is behaving suspiciously.

clue.text: Socially acceptable for lines to close

parts.note: U means upper-class, so socially acceptable
pro means in favour of
abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Proper lines for ending a letter politely.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproll is to roll up, as a scroll or blind is rolled shut.

clue.text: Kissed loudly by setter

indicators.note: doing something loudly suggests it is heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: to peck is to give a quick kiss
by, as in by day, means in

explanation.surface: The crossword setter gives a noisy smooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, but it is anything that makes jam set.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the substance in fruit that makes jams and jellies set firm.

clue.text: Hip mobile? Certain

indicators.note: mobile letters are free to move into a new order

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
one, as in 'one day', means a certain

explanation.surface: Is a trendy phone a sure thing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' works twice: it shuffles the word before it and also defines the phone, as the question mark warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPhone is Apple's smartphone, one well-known make of mobile.

clue.text: Take off from Orly one full of pluck

indicators.note: a word full of another word holds it inside

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport, so one in French
to pluck or fleece someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A brave passenger flies out of a Paris airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' and the airport suggest flying, but the definition means undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrobe is to take off one's robe or clothes, to undress.

clue.text: Vessels which heat running water for locals bordering Tunisia

indicators.note: bordering something on both sides surrounds it

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river, so streams are eas
international vehicle code for Tunisia

explanation.surface: Pots used by people near Tunisia to warm water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' seems to belong to the vessels' job, but it is part of the wordplay: 'locals' says the word for a stream is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: An etna is a small vessel for heating liquids over a spirit lamp, named after the volcano.

clue.text: Sections of Divine Comedy dismiss endless twaddle

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is removed

parts.note: to can someone is US slang for firing them
tosh is nonsense

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses parts of Dante's poem as unending drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Divine Comedy is divided into one hundred cantos, the main divisions of a long poem.

clue.text: These gemstones are ordinary, straight up

parts.note: standard abbreviation for ordinary

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: slap means directly, as in slap in the middle

explanation.surface: A jeweller says frankly that these stones are nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones made of silica.

clue.text: Translator of one of Plato's letters rings

parts.note: tr. is the abbreviation for translator
o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A translator of Plato's letters telephones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like Plato's epistles; it is the Greek alphabet, and 'rings' looks like a verb but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Trochi is the plural of trochus, meaning a wheel or hoop, so a ring.

clue.text: Break in congress muffled whirling hum of happiness …

indicators.note: a sound muffled by something is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: it is a euphemism for sex, sexual congress

indicators.note: whirling round turns something to face the opposite way

parts.note: a contented cat makes this sound

explanation.surface: A disruption in parliament quashed a buzz of contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like a legislature; here it is sexual congress, and the hum of happiness is a cat's.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or break in suddenly and violently.

clue.text: … and indeed, perversely nasty too (8, three words)

indicators.note: acting perversely means going against the expected order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the break-in was also deliberately nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Not to say introduces a stronger word, as in 'unwise, not to say reckless', meaning and indeed.

clue.text: Dead-beat | comprehensive (5, two words)

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both completely worn out and inclusive of all charges or items.

clue.text: Extra big shot apiece

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or important person
in scores, two all means two apiece

explanation.surface: An additional powerful shot for each person.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat; 'big shot' sounds like batting but means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery that gives the batting side an extra run.

clue.text: Joukery-pawkery is unknown in loch where monster lives

parts.note: 's is the short form of is

indicators.note: something in another thing is placed inside it

parts.note: L for loch, then Ness, home of the monster
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A Scots word for trickery hidden at Loch Ness, where Nessie lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Y sits between L and NESS. Joukery-pawkery is Scots for trickery or jiggery-pokery.
explanation.definitionFit: Joukery-pawkery means crafty trickery, which is cunning or slyness.

clue.text: Good to learn about English roasting birds

parts.note: standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: to see is to learn or find out
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: It is useful to learn about English birds cooked at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are birds traditionally roasted for a festive meal.
